title: 1965 AHSME Problem 4
statement: Line \(l_2\) intersects line \(l_1\) and line \(l_3\) is parallel to \(l_1.\) The three lines are distinct and lie in a plane. The number of points equidistant from all three lines is:

solutions.text:
Points equidistant from parallel lines \(l_1\) and \(l_3\) lie on the unique line midway between them. Points equidistant from intersecting lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) lie on either of their two angle bisectors. Each angle bisector meets the midway parallel once, giving two points.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Points equidistant from the two parallel lines lie on their midway parallel
Intersect that midway line with the two angle bisectors of \(l_1\) and \(l_2\)
